meta.title: U.S. regional planning modules
meta.warning: These are broad planning archetypes, not county-level forecasts. Validate them against local data before making decisions.

regions.label: Pacific Northwest
regions.profile: Coastal, river, mountain, forest, and dense urban systems with long-distance transport dependencies.
first72: Identify earthquake-safe shelter locations and utility shutoff knowledge.
Keep water, sanitation, medication, lighting, and charging independent of grid power.
Have a smoke/air-quality plan and a separate coastal or inland relocation decision.
Expect bridges, mountain routes, ports, and communications to be condition-dependent.
days14: Plan for pharmacy, fuel, water, and food disruptions without assuming a quick resupply.
Use two geographically separated family meeting options.
Track official evacuation zones, road closures, smoke, and water advisories.
months: Prepare for housing, employment, school, insurance, and medical continuity if a regional corridor is disrupted.
Maintain a resupply relationship outside the immediate neighborhood.
validation: FEMA National Risk Index at county and tract level
NOAA and National Weather Service alerts

regions.label: California & Great Basin
regions.profile: Large urban corridors, drought and heat exposure, wildfire interfaces, mountain passes, and complex water and power dependencies.
first72: Separate wildfire evacuation planning from earthquake shelter-in-place planning.
Build for heat and smoke when grid power or cooling is unavailable.
Keep multiple routes and a fuel decision rule; do not depend on one pass, freeway, or bridge.
Protect medication, documents, water, and communication devices from heat and power loss.
days14: Plan for water, cooling, fuel, and pharmacy constraints.
Designate an out-of-area contact and a backup household location.
Pre-decide when to leave before official routes become congested.
months: Model insurance, housing, employment, and long-term displacement options.
Map alternate medical providers and supply sources outside the affected corridor.
validation: CAL FIRE or relevant state fire agencies

regions.label: Southwest
regions.states: Arizona · New Mexico · southern Nevada · west Texas
regions.profile: Heat, drought, long distances, water constraints, wildfire, and concentrated urban infrastructure.
first72: Treat water, cooling, and power as linked life-safety dependencies.
Keep a shaded or climate-controlled fallback location in mind.
Plan vehicle, fuel, and communications around long distances.
Use official heat, air-quality, and flood alerts rather than visual judgment alone.
days14: Plan for refrigeration, medication, water refill, and cooling-center access.
Identify a second route and a second destination outside the local utility footprint.
Account for outdoor workers, older adults, children, and pets.
months: Model employment, water restrictions, housing, and medical continuity.
Maintain a resupply option in a different watershed or utility area where practical.
validation: National Weather Service heat and flood products

regions.label: Rockies & High Plains
regions.states: Montana · Wyoming · Colorado · Utah · western Dakotas · eastern Idaho
regions.profile: Mountain and rural access constraints, severe winter, wildfire, drought, long travel distances, and transportation chokepoints.
first72: Plan for isolation and blocked roads rather than assuming nearby services remain reachable.
Keep heat, water, communications, and vehicle readiness independent of one system.
Monitor fire, weather, road, and avalanche information as separate inputs.
Prepare for livestock, pets, and rural medical-distance problems where applicable.
days14: Keep a resupply and medical plan for prolonged road closures.
Identify a warm, powered fallback location.
Use redundant navigation and contact methods.
months: Model employment, housing, school, and medical relocation if a corridor remains closed.
Build relationships with neighboring households and local emergency managers.

regions.label: Great Plains & Midwest
regions.states: Nebraska · Kansas · Oklahoma · Iowa · Missouri · Minnesota · Wisconsin · Illinois · Indiana · Michigan · Ohio
regions.profile: Severe weather, river and lake systems, winter conditions, agricultural and rail dependencies, and large geographic exposure.
first72: Have a safe-room or shelter plan and a way to receive warnings when power or cellular service is impaired.
Prepare for simultaneous power, road, and water interruptions.
Keep weather radio or another independent alert path.
Know which local roads flood, close, or become impassable.
days14: Plan for fuel, food, pharmacy, and payment disruption after a major storm.
Use an out-of-area contact because local networks may be overloaded.
Account for seasonal heating or cooling needs.
months: Model housing, employment, school, crop or food-system effects, and insurance recovery.
Identify alternate regional supply and medical centers.

regions.label: Gulf Coast & Southeast
regions.states: Texas Gulf · Louisiana · Mississippi · Alabama · Georgia · Florida · South Carolina · North Carolina · Tennessee
regions.profile: Hurricanes, storm surge, inland flooding, heat, dense coastal infrastructure, and long recovery timelines.
first72: Decide early whether the plan is shelter, local relocation, or evacuation; waiting reduces options.
Protect documents, medications, water, communications, and vehicle fuel.
Use official evacuation zones and routes, not informal map shortcuts.
Prepare for heat and humidity if power fails.
days14: Plan for fuel scarcity, water advisories, pharmacy interruptions, and debris-blocked roads.
Have a destination outside the hazard and a way to verify it is open.
Account for mold, heat, medical access, and pets after the immediate event.
months: Model displacement, insurance, housing, employment, school, and long-term medical needs.
Keep records and resupply contacts outside the affected coastal area.
validation: National Hurricane Center and National Weather Service

regions.label: Mid-Atlantic & Northeast
regions.states: Virginia · Maryland · Delaware · District of Columbia · Pennsylvania · New Jersey · New York · New England
regions.profile: Dense population, coastal and river exposure, aging infrastructure, winter weather, heat, and high interdependence between metro systems.
first72: Plan for sheltering in dense housing and loss of elevators, transit, water pressure, or communications.
Keep a walkable local option and an out-of-area contact.
Separate flood, storm, winter, and heat plans; they create different movement constraints.
Protect medication, cash, documents, and charging access.
days14: Plan for transit, fuel, pharmacy, childcare, and building-access disruption.
Identify alternate work, school, and medical arrangements.
Use official emergency alerts and local authority guidance.
months: Model housing, employment, school, insurance, and medical displacement.
Consider the effects of regional congestion and limited hotel capacity.
validation: National Weather Service coastal and winter products
Local transit and utility outage information

regions.label: Alaska
regions.profile: Large distances, limited road connectivity, severe cold, earthquake and tsunami exposure, aviation and marine dependencies.
first72: Prioritize heat, water, shelter, communications, and location-specific evacuation knowledge.
Assume that roads, ports, or aircraft may be unavailable.
Keep a local plan and a remote-contact plan.
Account for cold-weather medical and vehicle risks.
days14: Plan for air and marine resupply delay, fuel, medication, and heating needs.
Maintain more than one communications method where feasible.
Coordinate with local, tribal, and state emergency-management guidance.
months: Model seasonal access, relocation, employment, schooling, and medical evacuation.
Treat resupply distance as a primary planning variable.
validation: FEMA National Risk Index where available
Alaska state and local emergency-management guidance

regions.label: Hawaii & Pacific territories
regions.profile: Island and remote logistics, volcanic and tsunami exposure, hurricanes, wildfire, limited redundancy, and dependence on maritime and air supply.
first72: Know local evacuation zones and vertical or inland options where applicable.
Treat water, power, fuel, communications, and medical access as linked dependencies.
Keep a plan for island-specific movement restrictions.
Use local official alerts and do not rely on mainland assumptions.
days14: Plan for maritime and air resupply delay, pharmacy continuity, and fuel scarcity.
Maintain local mutual-aid contacts and an out-of-area communications contact.
Protect documents and medical supplies from heat, moisture, and displacement.
months: Model long-distance relocation, housing, employment, schooling, and medical continuity.
Treat transportation availability as a strategic constraint.
validation: FEMA National Risk Index where available
